note: A tree with invented joins in it is worse than no tree, so none of these has any. Each line is drawn in the form its own evidence supports.

rows.name: Booyzen
rows.depth: The Cape Dutch line the archive carries
rows.what: Graaff-Reinet, Cradock, Barkly East, then off the train at Johannesburg with nothing. The family changed one letter of its name in a war and kept the new spelling.

rows.name: Kolbe
rows.depth: London, 1802 — a gravestone in the Karoo that agrees with it, and nine children of the Free State house
rows.what: George Augustus Kolbe was born in Soho and sailed from Gravesend at sixteen, turning seventeen at sea. His stone at Burgersdorp gives 7 December 1802, and two hundred years later somebody found the London church book, which gives the same day. His eldest son commanded the Bloemfontein district and died on the farm Leeuwberg in 1868 leaving eight sons and four daughters, none of them named in his obituary; nine were found in September 2026 by searching the fonts on their mother's name rather than his.
rows.gap: Still no chart, but the house is drawn: nine of the Commandant's twelve are now named from baptism registers and civil death registrations, and the household is at /households/. Three of the twelve are missing and the obituary is the only authority for the count.

rows.name: Barry
rows.depth: An Overberg merchant house, or a common surname — not settled
rows.what: The name recurs in the archive and the connection to the Overberg Barrys is suggestive and unproved. The archive says so rather than claiming it.
rows.gap: No chart, and no join established.

rows.name: The British women
rows.depth: Downing · van Jaarsveld · Mountjoy · Schoeman and the rest
rows.what: A Cape Dutch family that kept marrying British women. The lines that join it are the shape of the whole archive, not a footnote to it.

close: The form is checked, not asserted: a line counts as drawn only where this archive actually publishes a chart of it.

origins._note: One origin label per line, in the words the other archives use (documented / origin inferred / origin unknown). Each is only what this archive's own pages already say; the counts beside it are computed from people.json in trees.astro. kind is documented, inferred or unknown.

Booyzen.text: the chart stops at generation 7, at a man with no dates and no parents (The Spine)

Kolbe.text: London, 1802; a gravestone at Burgersdorp and the London church book give the same day

Barry.text: an Overberg merchant house or a common surname, not settled, and no join established

Mountjoy.text: the earliest man on the line, born “Europe” about 1782, has his parents entered as not known on his death notice

Daschner.text: the earliest, born at Stutterheim about 1883, has his father and mother named on his 1942 death notice and no dates for either

Olivier.text: the earliest dated was baptised at Cradock in 1820; his parents are named, undated, on an 1891 death notice

Pretorius.text: a wife, her father and two more of the name, the men undated

Schoeman.text: four people, none with a birth or death date, around a man of Barkly Oost whose daughter married into the Barrys

Downing.text: the one Downing born in London in 1803 is documented; her father is on the family tree and in no document this archive has read

Lerena.text: three people here; the Lerena family has its own archive

McCabe.text: one woman, born about 1855, who married into the Kolbes at Bloemfontein in 1872; no parent is entered on the line

notPlaced.note: People are never unplaced here: every one of the people.json entries carries exactly one line. What is not placed is the register's raw catch, and one cluster the archive has tested and could not settle. Counts are computed from register.json; the claim count for Marico is the one the atlas states.
